summary: This PR adds a ReviewBench evaluation harness (new src/evaluation/* modules for corpus preparation, retries, replay, scoring and adjudication), makes the reviewer pipeline more failure-aware (provider streaming/timeouts/usage records, two-stage result object with stage status, deep/triage changes) and lands a large volume of evaluation artifacts, datasets and docs. The reviewer work is mostly inside src/reviewer and src/analyzer, while the new evaluation code under src/evaluation is where correctness of the harness (diff parsing, status labeling, candidate/finding matching, scoring) must be checked, since results produced there are used as the project's quality evidence.

critic_decisions.title: Every ordinary modification is labeled RENAMED because there is no MODIFIED branch
critic_decisions.reason:
The patch contradicts the premise. The supplied new-file code contains the complete four-branch ternary:

    status = (
        FileStatus.REMOVED
        if new == "/dev/null"
        else FileStatus.ADDED
        if old == "/dev/null"
        else FileStatus.RENAMED
        if old[2:] != new[2:]
        else FileStatus.MODIFIED
    )

So the comparison `old[2:] != new[2:]` the candidate says is "never made" IS made, and a MODIFIED branch exists. That `status` value is consumed immediately by `ChangedFile(..., status=status, previous_filename=old[2:] if status == FileStatus.RENAMED else None, ...)`, so an ordinary edit (neither side /dev/null and old[2:]==new[2:]) resolves to MODIFIED, not RENAMED. The candidate's own recommendation is verbatim what the patch already implements. The failure scenario (all edits labeled RENAMED, MODIFIED path unreachable) cannot follow from this code.

critic_decisions.title: Critic replay re-attaches findings by identity, so findings for removed suggestions can survive
critic_decisions.reason: The code does build `keys = {(s.file_path, s.line, s.title) for s in kept}` (a set) and then re-attaches findings by testing that same identity tuple per suggestion, so the mapping is genuinely lossy for duplicate identity tuples: if two baseline suggestions share (file_path,line,title) and only one is in `kept`, the removed one's finding would also pass the `in keys` test and be copied. However, whether that state is reachable is not decidable from this patch alone. The scenario requires (a) duplicate-identity suggestions in the baseline and (b) `apply_critic`/`select_critic_candidates` removing exactly one of them. If removal is keyed by identity (plausible, given the surrounding pure-identity handling) both duplicates drop together and no bug occurs; removal semantics live in `apply_critic`, which is not in the supplied patch. The mechanism the candidate describes is real, but the triggering condition is unverified, so this is not confirmable as a concrete failure.

pending_suggestions.reason: After the Critic runs, `keys = {(s.file_path, s.line, s.title) for s in kept}` is a set, and the replay loop appends `finding` whenever the source suggestion's (file_path, line, title) is in that set. Positional pairing is lost: if two baseline suggestions share the same identity tuple (duplicate model output, e.g. the same title on the same line), `keys` collapses them, so when the Critic removes one of them the removed suggestion's finding is still copied into the replay candidate. The candidate JSON then contradicts the Critic `decisions` that were just computed, inflating the measured effect of the Critic.
pending_suggestions.recommendation:
Match positionally instead of by identity, e.g. have apply_critic return kept indices (or compute `removed_indices` and filter with enumerate):
```python
for i, (suggestion, finding) in enumerate(zip(suggestions, old_output["findings"])):
    if i not in removed_indices:
        output_findings.append(finding)
```
and assert len(suggestions) == len(old_output["findings"]) up front so the strict zip cannot abort the run mid-way.
pending_suggestions.failure_scenario: A baseline case contains two identical-identity suggestions on the same line (duplicate generations). apply_critic removes one; because `keys` is a set the surviving suggestion re-adds both findings to the replay candidate, so the Critic ablation reports a finding as retained although the Critic removed it, and the produced candidate JSON no longer agrees with the recorded removal decisions.
